decisions.claim: B has a 3.5 percent share (in a company)
decisions.reason: Directly stated via 'Your 3.5 percent share' — the possessive 'Your' establishes B holds this share.

decisions.claim: B's 3.5 percent share is going to be worth at least a million
decisions.reason: This is A's future prediction/opinion about the share's value, not a confirmed attribute of B. A could be wrong or exaggerating.
decisions.counterexample: B could reply: 'I don't believe it will be worth that much.'

decisions.claim: B has the option to leave (the company/deal)
decisions.reason: 'If you leave' presupposes B has the option to leave. This is a necessary inference from the conditional.

decisions.claim: If B leaves, B will make nothing
decisions.reason: This is A's conditional prediction about consequences, not an established fact about B. A may be bluffing or incorrect about the outcome.
decisions.counterexample: B could reply: 'I'd still have my share and could sell it elsewhere.'

decisions.claim: B can sign the Stars.com account
decisions.reason: 'If you sign the Stars.com account' presupposes B has the ability/authority to sign it.

decisions.claim: B is in competition with WebTracker for the Stars.com account
decisions.reason: 'before WebTracker does' presupposes both B and WebTracker are competing to sign the Stars.com account.

decisions.claim: B holds a 3.5 percent share in a business or asset
decisions.reason: Identical content to c1 — B holds a 3.5 percent share. 'In a business or asset' is the same as 'in a company' at this granularity.

decisions.claim: B is in a position to accept or reject a deal offered by A
decisions.reason: B's question 'What if I said no?' and A's response 'You wouldn't!' together establish B is in a position to accept or reject a deal offered by A.

decisions.claim: B has the option to leave the current arrangement
decisions.reason: Same presupposition from the same quote 'If you leave' — B has the option to leave the arrangement.

decisions.claim: B is currently making money from the arrangement
decisions.reason: 'You'll make nothing' if B leaves does not necessarily mean B is currently making money; it could mean B is currently positioned to make money in the future. The inference is too speculative.
decisions.counterexample: B could reply: 'I haven't made a dime yet; I was just hoping to.'

decisions.claim: B has the authority to sign the Stars.com account
decisions.reason: Same presupposition from 'If you sign the Stars.com account' — B has the authority/ability to sign it.

decisions.claim: B's share is projected by A to be worth at least a million
decisions.reason: This is A's projection, not a confirmed attribute of B. Even framed as 'projected by A,' it's not a fact about B's situation but about A's opinion.
decisions.counterexample: B could reply: 'You've said that before and it hasn't panned out.'

design: dual route, targeted rescue, globally grouped evidence adjudication
